summary: Assistance requested: safe live-snapshot and rollback plan after enabling aggressive batching + quant profiles
description:
Issue summary:
Customer enabled an aggressive optimizer bundle (continuous batching: high_batch_size, kv_prefetch, and q4 quant profile) on their Dedicated pool during a traffic ramp. Within ~30 minutes they saw elevated 95p tail latency and occasional 502s for tenant traffic. Customer is asking for: (1) step-by-step safe live snapshot of current optimizer state per-tenant, and (2) an immediate rollback plan that can be executed with minimal traffic disruption and no model unpinning.

Impact:
- Intermittent 502 errors for ~2% of requests for NexaLabs production traffic.
- Customer-facing latency SLA breaches (95p latency increased from 130ms -> 820ms).
- Business: serving degradation during peak window; customer requests assisted rollback to stable baseline.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) for NexaLabs, prod, us-east region.
- Recent change: optimizer profile "nlp-aggr-batch-v7" applied at 2026-03-12T10:40Z.

Requested outcome:
- A reproducible safe snapshot of the current optimizer configuration that can be restored if needed.
- A rollback procedure that minimizes request loss and preserves pinned model versions.

Attachments: links to latency dashboard and sample request ids included in comments.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Apply optimizer profile nlp-aggr-batch-v7 to tenant NexaLabs in dedicated pool.
2) Route production traffic (steady ramp to 80% of committed throughput).
3) Observe tail latency and 502 spikes within 20-40 minutes.
4) Errors appear correlated with longer sequences (>512 tokens) and bursty concurrent requests.
logs:
Sample 502 trace IDs: trx-20260312-11-7f3a, trx-20260312-11-9b1d. Server log excerpts: 
[2026-03-12T11:02:34Z] serving-runtime ERROR tenant=nexalabs request=trx-20260312-11-7f3a upstream=worker-3 code=502 message=upstream-unavailable kernel-oom?=false mem-usage=86%
[2026-03-12T11:07:12Z] scheduler WARN autoscaler delayed-batch-fill reason=kv-prefetch-lock contention=high
Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tenant-nexalabs/optimizer-metrics?from=1640&to=1680
investigation_notes:
Initial triage by Support: confirmed correlation between optimizer enable time and latency increase. Hypothesis: aggressive batching + kv_prefetch is increasing lock contention on GPU memory paths for mixed-precision kernels under this workload shape (long sequences + multi-stream concurrency). Autoscaler configuration (burst windows) appears to be tuned for lower batch sizes and is not adding capacity fast enough. Observed increased scheduler queueing and more frequent model cold-starts as KV cache eviction churn increased.
Actions taken so far:
- Collected heap and GPU memory samples from affected workers.
- Captured optimizer config snapshot (id: snap-2026-03-12-nlpaudit) and stored under tenant snapshot store.
- Scoped the effect to tenant NexaLabs only (no cluster-wide degradation).
comments: 2026-03-12 | Sofia Martinez (Support): Customer reports 502 spikes and higher tail latency after applying 'nlp-aggr-batch-v7' optimizer profile at ~10:40Z. Asking for assisted safe rollback. SLA flagged.

2026-03-12 | On-call SRE (Miguel Rivera): pulled logs and GPU metrics. Noted scheduler queue depth spike and kv-prefetch lock contention. Recommended creating optimizer snapshot immediately before rolling back.

2026-03-12 | Liam Patel (Support/SE): Created snapshot snap-2026-03-12-nlpaudit and uploaded to tenant store. Suggested staged rollback: 1) reduce batch target, 2) disable kv_prefetch, 3) monitor 5-minute windows, 4) if stable, restore baseline profile. Asked customer if they can tolerate a short traffic split.

2026-03-12 | NexaLabs (Customer - Priya Sinha): Prefer no model unpinning and minimal disruption. Can accept 10% traffic split for 15 minutes during a low-traffic window. Wants exact CLI commands and runbook steps.
2026-03-13 | Liam Patel (Support): Posted runbook below and will coordinate a 10:30Z maintenance window. Assigned to On-call SRE for execution assistance.
runbook_steps:
Preflight (5 mins): verify snapshot exists (snap-2026-03-12-nlpaudit) and confirm traffic window.
1) Create a 10% traffic split to a fallback route that uses optimizer profile 'baseline-v3' (CLI: redwood route split --tenant nexalabs --from-profile nlp-aggr-batch-v7 --to-profile baseline-v3 --percent 10).
2) Wait 5 minutes and check 95p latency and 502 rate; collect traces.
3) If metrics improve, increase split to 50% for 5 minutes; if stable, increase to 100% and decommission 'nlp-aggr-batch-v7' on tenant.
4) If at any step errors increase, immediately revert split by setting 0% to the baseline route and open incident.
5) To fully restore previous optimizer state, use snapshot restore: redwood optimizer restore --tenant nexalabs --snapshot snap-2026-03-12-nlpaudit (note: snapshot restore is safe but will not change model pinning).
resolution_notes: Workaround provided: guided staged traffic split and snapshot-based fallback. Customer executed 10% split at 2026-03-13T10:30Z with Support/SRE on call. 95p latency dropped to 160ms and 502s reduced to <0.1% within first 5 minutes. Proceeding with gradual ramp; plan to complete full rollback and close ticket after 24h stability window. Follow-up: recommend adjusting autoscaler burst settings and reducing target_batch_size for long-sequence workloads.
root_cause: Aggressive optimizer profile combined with tenant workload shape (long sequences, burst concurrency) created KV cache eviction and kernel memory contention. Autoscaler response lagged given current burst windows, amplifying tail latency and transient 502s.
postmortem_actions:
- Update tenant onboarding docs to include guidance for long-sequence workloads and optimizer tuning.
- Add a preflight simulator check in Console: 'optimizer stress check' to predict contention for given profile.
- Engineering task (linked): tune autoscaler heuristics for mixed-precision + kv_prefetch scenarios (track via PR #3214).
next_steps:
1) Complete full rollback to baseline-v3 and monitor 24h.
2) Schedule postmortem with NexaLabs and product to discuss safer rollout guardrails.
3) Create a KB article for customers: 'Safe live snapshot & rollback for optimizer changes'.
estimated_customer_impact: Partial impairment (2% error rate during peak) resolved after staged rollback; customer experienced a brief SLA window but no data loss.
